target.output: allocator collision retry policy and burst-race evidence

problem: Identical workers can repeatedly select opportunities that were claimed moments after their snapshot and then lose create-if-absent races. The tested allocator excludes already-active claims, but its published evidence does not define or measure bounded post-collision refresh/retry, anti-starvation or burst-contention behavior.
acceptance: burst canary with at least 20 contenders yields bounded claim attempts per worker and no overwrite
collision loser refreshes the durable frontier before retry and does not immediately hammer the same target
fairness or anti-starvation policy is documented and tested under deterministic replay
idle or discovery is entered only after refreshed prepared, recovery and dynamically-ready frontiers are exhausted
title: Allocator contention backoff and fairness canary
mission: Add a candidate-only contention policy and deterministic burst canary for the universal worker allocator. After an exclusive claim loss, force a durable-frontier refresh before reselection, bound repeated attempts, prevent immediate same-target hammering, and record fairness/starvation metrics across at least 20 identical contenders without weakening create-if-absent exclusivity or authority boundaries.

human_friction_reduction.reason: Broad identical-worker launches should not require the human to compensate for repeated claim collisions or manually reroute workers.

regression_prevention.reason: A burst policy can preserve exclusive mutation while preventing a thundering-herd retry pattern from turning safe collision handling into low useful throughput.

information_gain.reason: A 20+ contender deterministic canary would measure post-collision behavior that the current 11-test allocator receipt does not cover.

fail_if: any loser overwrites an existing claim
a worker retries the same target without refreshing durable claim state
bounded retry policy causes useful unclaimed work to be skipped
deterministic replay can starve one eligible worker indefinitely
allocator self-promotes proposal/candidate output to READY, Current, Human Accepted or Served
